To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a diet rich in HT from day 100 of age to slaughter reduced salivary and bulbo-urethral glands size, but did not affect the sensory evaluation of boar meat.
a diet supplemented with 30 g/kg of hydrolysable tanning reduced skatole level and the size of accessory sex glands in group-housed entire male pigs.
a diet rich in HT has no effect on growth performance, has a minimal impact in reducing boar taint but reduces the size of salivary and the bulbourethral glands of entire male pigs.

the impact of HT-rich diet on growth performance, boar tainting and hepatic gene expression of boar tainting-related CYP isoenzimes.
the effect of HT on the development of accessory glands and on the metabolism of indolic substances and androstenol.
a group of HT that are not toxic, have a low impact on feed intake and performance and are able to reduce skatole and androstenol concentrations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HT have a limited impact on growth performance and carcass characteristics, but may reduce boar taint in EM.
HT have a minimal impact on the performance of entire boars and may reduce the risk of boar taint.
HT had no negative effects on growth performance, meat quality and carcass characteristics of group-housed EM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HT have a minimal impact on performance but significantly reduce the size of accessory sex glands and thus the risk of boar taint.
HT may be used to control boar taint in group-housed EM.
HT are less detrimental to growth performance and boar tainting compared with CT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HT have a minimal impact on growth performance and carcass traits of entire male pigs, but may be effective in reducing boar taint.
HT may have a potential to reduce boar taint in group housed EM.
HT may be used in diets of entire male pigs at levels of up to 30 g/kg without compromising performance and carcass traits.
